extra.message: User-controlled parameter 'username' is interpolated directly into an f-string SQL query passed to 'run_sql_query' without any sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g., 'username=" OR 1=1; --"', to extract, modify, or destroy data.

User-supplied fields from the 'User' Pydantic model (name, username, password, address, email, contact) are interpolated directly into an INSERT SQL query via f-string at lines 188-204. An attacker can inject SQL in any of these fields, e.g., address=\"\"); DROP TABLE users; --\" to execute arbitrary SQL on insertion.

The query parameter 'username' (line 229-232) and 'user.address' (line 234-235) are interpolated directly into DELETE SQL queries via f-strings without sanitization. An attacker can drop or manipulate any row, e.g., username='\" OR 1=1; DELETE FROM users; --'.

User-controlled 'username' parameter is used directly as a dict key to query the MontyClient (NoSQL-like) database at line 220. While this does not produce classic NoSQL operator injection because the value is matched for equality rather than passed as a query document, the input is still unsanitized. If a POST body is provided via /find, the query is completely user-controlled.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a NoSQL Command

extra.message: The POST /find endpoint directly parses the entire request body as JSON (line 224: await request.json()) and passes it wholesale to get_nosql_users() for use as a query document in db_client.vfapi.users.find(). An attacker can construct arbitrary query documents like {"$gt": ""} containing NoSQL operator injection to bypass authentication or extract all user records, including passwords stored in the NoSQL collection.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a NoSQL Command

extra.message: The application uses MD5 for password hashing (imported at line 13, used at lines 113, 187). MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash algorithm that is vulnerable to collision attacks and trivial brute-force cracking via rainbow tables. Passwords should instead be hashed with a strong slow hash function such as argon2, bcrypt, or scrypt with proper salt.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The get_nosql_users function removes internal fields ('_id' and 'password') from NoSQL user documents before returning them (line 172). While this prevents exposure of the password field, the SQL-based endpoints (GET /select, PUT /user, DELETE /user) do NOT filter out the password from SQL results. If a SQL injection succeeds in retrieving the full SQL query results, the MD5-hashed (and plaintext in the NoSQL) passwords are exposed.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The endpoint /select (line 180), which queries the entire users table by username (line 182), has no authentication or authorization requirements. Any unauthenticated, anonymous user can retrieve user records including potentially sensitive fields. This applies to all user-related endpoints (PUT /user, GET /find, POST /find, DELETE /user) as well.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The Swagger UI HTML response at line 263 concatenates 'app.title' directly into the HTML page title without escaping. If app.title is user-controllable or settable at runtime, an attacker could inject cross-site scripting (XSS) content. While FastAPI's app.title is a developer-supplied constant here, the construction pattern using string concatenation for HTML content (no CSP headers either) is inherently unsafe in general.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: The POST /reset endpoint (line 242) uses os.remove() and shutil.rmtree() to delete the entire SQL and NoSQL database files on every request. There is no authentication, authorization, or confirmation. Any anonymous user can reset the entire database by issuing a POST request to /reset, causing a denial of service for all users.

The /redoc endpoint (line 265) and /docs endpoint (line 261) load OpenAPI JSON and Swagger specs from publicly-accessible URLs via external Google Fonts (line 268: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Montserrat:300,400,700|Roboto:300,400,700') with no Content-Security-Policy, referrer-policy, or security headers configured. The swagger UI is exposed at /docs for all unauthenticated users.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in 'Secure' HTTP Cookie Without 'Secure' Attribute
